newsitem.title: USA: Calif. transit district OKs $1.2 bln rail plan.
newsitem.headline: Calif. transit district OKs $1.2 bln rail plan.

text.p: Northern California's Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) District on Thursday approved the lease agreement for a proposed $1.167 billion rail extension project, BART said.

The BART board of directors voted 7-to-2 to approve the agreement, which allows BART to build rail facilities at San Francisco International Airport and calls for the transit district to pay an annual rent of $2.5 million for 50 years.
The lease agreement was a crucial part of the proposed 8.7-mile, $1.167 billion project extending BART to San Francisco International, local officials said.
The lease agreement was needed in order for the federal government to release $750 million for the project, the officials said.
On Wednesday, the San Francisco Board of Supervisors approved a resolution that calls for the city to back the lease agreement between BART and the airport.
Under the resolution, San Francisco will ensure that BART pays its rent in full to the airport. Should BART default, the city would redirect transit funding to cover the lease payments.
Last week, the San Francisco Airport Commission approved the lease agreement.
